recent_posts.title: April 2026: GPT-5.5, Opus 4.7, DeepSeek V4, AI Trust Issues, Patrol MCP
recent_posts.summary: A monthly newsletter covering April 2026 AI and Flutter developments. Three major model launches shipped: GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, and DeepSeek V4. Despite record benchmark scores, developer trust in AI tools is declining due to real-world quality degradation and stricter usage limits. DeepSeek V4 is highlighted for its agent-optimized architecture and 1M context window at lower cost. Flutter news includes the Material/Cupertino code freeze moving those packages out of the SDK, and Dart/Flutter's AI strategy for 2026. Patrol MCP is introduced as a way for AI agents to write and run E2E tests on mobile apps. The author also promotes their Agentic Coding Toolkit for Flutter.

recent_posts.title: March 2026: Flutter's 2026 roadmap, GPT-5.4, agentic workflows, AI orchestration, safer coding agents
recent_posts.summary: A curated newsletter covering March 2026 developments in Flutter and AI-assisted coding. Key highlights include Flutter & Dart's 2026 roadmap (Impeller migration, WebAssembly, AI tooling, full-stack Dart), the preview of Genkit for Dart, GPT-5.4's launch with 1M-token context, and a survey showing 87% of developers still use at most two agents. The edition dives into agentic workflow philosophy (specs vs. code), AI orchestration tools like 'cook', flutter-skill for AI-driven E2E UI testing, and safety tools like Claude Code auto mode and 'nah' for context-aware permission guards. The author also launches ACT (Agentic Coding Toolkit), a spec-driven workflow product for Flutter/Dart development with Claude Code.

recent_posts.title: February 2026: Flutter 3.41, 16 Claudes Build a C Compiler, the OpenClaw Security Crisis, and GPT-5.3 Codex
recent_posts.summary: A February 2026 developer newsletter covering Flutter 3.41 and Dart 3.11 releases, Anthropic's experiment using 16 Claude instances to build a C compiler in Rust (~$20K, 100K lines, 99% test pass rate) with caveats about misleading marketing, OpenAI's GPT-5.3-Codex launch enabling 8+ hour autonomous coding tasks, and the OpenClaw security crisis where a popular AI agent with 230K GitHub stars exposed 40K+ instances, distributed malware via its marketplace, and triggered a supply chain attack on Cline CLI. Also covers opinion pieces on the SDLC being replaced by tight AI feedback loops, the importance of documentation artifacts (PRDs, ADRs, TDDs) for AI-assisted development, and the argument that code is now cheap but meaningful software is not.

recent_posts.title: January 2026: AI Agents Take Over, Claude Code Workflows, Multi-Agent Orchestration, and OpenCode
recent_posts.summary: AI coding agents have reached a maturity threshold as of December 2025, fundamentally changing software development workflows. Claude Code and alternatives like OpenCode enable developers to work primarily in natural language, running multiple parallel agent sessions with varying levels of automation. Key workflows include Boris Cherny's multi-session approach with Plan Mode and verification loops, Steve Yegge's Gas Town orchestration system for 20-30 parallel agents, and Geoffrey Huntley's simple Ralph bash loop technique. Anthropic recently blocked third-party tools from using subscription tokens, sparking community backlash. The shift moves developers from imperative coding to declarative success criteria, with experienced practitioners like Andrej Karpathy noting they now code 80% through agents and Peter Steinberger claiming he no longer reads generated code.

recent_posts.title: December 2025: Flutter GenUI SDK, Build Runner Speedups, 2025 LLM Year in Review
recent_posts.summary: Flutter's AI ecosystem expanded in 2025 with the GenUI SDK for AI-generated UIs, the Flutter AI Toolkit v1.0, and MCP server integration. The Flutter team is decoupling Material and Cupertino libraries from the core framework, with separate pub.dev packages coming in 2026. Build runner received a major performance boost with 2x faster code generation through improved transitive import tracking. The broader AI landscape saw releases of GPT-5.2, Gemini 3, and Opus 4.5, while the Model Context Protocol became an open standard under the Linux Foundation. DevContainers offer a solution for safely running AI agents like Claude Code and Cursor in isolated environments without constant permission prompts.

recent_posts.title: How to Safely Run AI Agents Like Cursor and Claude Code Inside a DevContainer
recent_posts.summary: Running AI coding agents like Claude Code with permission prompts disabled poses security risks from prompt injection attacks. DevContainers provide a solution by isolating AI agents in Docker containers, allowing autonomous operation without endangering the host system. The guide demonstrates setting up a DevContainer with Flutter support, installing necessary extensions in VSCode/Cursor, and configuring Claude Code to run with the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag safely. The containerized environment handles code generation, terminal commands, and version control, while the host machine manages UI testing and debugging. This workflow shifts developers from supervising every AI action to defining tasks and reviewing results.

recent_posts.title: November 2025: Flutter 3.38, Dart 3.10, The AI Coding Wars (Gemini 3 vs Claude Opus 4.5)
recent_posts.summary: Flutter 3.38 and Dart 3.10 introduce dot shorthand syntax, 16KB Android page size support, and iOS 26 compatibility. Google launched Gemini 3 with their new Antigravity IDE, while Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.5 and OpenAI announced GPT 5.1 Codex models, intensifying competition in AI-powered development tools. Security researchers identified vulnerabilities in agentic coding tools, highlighting risks like data exfiltration and prompt injection. The piece includes a decision matrix for choosing between manual coding and AI assistance based on prompting versus coding effort.

recent_posts.title: When to Code vs Prompt with AI
recent_posts.summary: A practical framework for deciding when to use AI coding assistants versus writing code manually. Introduces a 2x2 decision matrix based on prompting effort versus coding effort, categorizing common Flutter development tasks into four quadrants. AI excels at boilerplate, tests, and localization (low prompt, high code), while direct coding is better for layout fixes and one-line changes (high prompt, low code). Complex features like offline syncing require iterative AI collaboration with careful human oversight. The key insight: choose between agentic AI and autocomplete based on task complexity and cognitive load.

recent_posts.title: October 2025: Flutter & Figma MCP, Platform & UI threads merge, Andrej Karpathy on AGI
recent_posts.summary: Monthly roundup covering Flutter's platform and UI thread merge in version 3.32, enabling synchronous native code calls. Highlights include a new MCP server for converting Figma designs to Flutter widgets, WebAssembly 3.0 release with garbage collection and 64-bit support, and FlutterCon EU 2025 videos. Also features Andrej Karpathy's perspective on AGI development timelines and AI-assisted coding workflows, plus a structured 3-folder system for effective AI-powered Flutter development.

recent_posts.title: Beyond Prompts: My 3-Folder System for Effective AI Coding in Flutter
recent_posts.summary: A structured approach to AI-assisted Flutter development using three dedicated folders: ai_toolkit for reusable commands and patterns, ai_specs for tracking prompts and implementation plans, and ai_docs for persistent project knowledge. This system helps maintain consistency, reduce friction, and improve code quality when working with AI coding agents by providing proper context and guardrails throughout the development workflow.
